findings.title: Reseed order: ReseedSilo reads stalkIssuedPerBdv before ReseedWhitelist sets it
findings.description: The reseed pipeline runs facet init() calls in a fixed sequence (reseed/reseed.js): reseed5 -> ReseedSilo.init, reseed6 -> ReseedInternalBalances.init, reseed7 -> ReseedWhitelist.init. ReseedSilo.reseedSiloDeposit computes each migrated account's base Stalk from `stalkIssuedPerBdv` read out of `s.sys.silo.assetSettings[siloDeposit.token].stalkIssuedPerBdv` (ReseedSilo.sol#112), then `accountStalk += stalkIssuedPerBdv * totalBdvForAccount` (#161) and `s.accts[account].stalk = accountStalk` (#164). However, `assetSettings[token].stalkIssuedPerBdv` is ONLY ever populated by LibWhitelist.whitelistToken (LibWhitelist.sol#161), which is invoked by ReseedWhitelist.init — two pipeline steps AFTER ReseedSilo. At the time ReseedSilo runs, assetSettings is still zero-initialized, so `stalkIssuedPerBdv` reads 0 for every token. The base-stalk term collapses to 0, and because the per-deposit grown-stalk term is also ~0 at reseed (every deposit's stem equals the supplied stemTip, so `stemTip - stem == 0` at #132), each migrated holder is reseeded with effectively zero Stalk. This is a cross-step state-consistency / lifecycle-ordering defect: state written in a later reseed step (asset settings) is a precondition for a calculation performed in an earlier step. It is distinct from the sibling logic findings (LG-002 stalk overwrite via `=`, LG-003 missing roots/global totals): even if those were fixed, the value being assigned would still be ~0 because the multiplicand is read before it is initialized.

location.code_snippet:
uint256 stalkIssuedPerBdv = s.sys.silo.assetSettings[siloDeposit.token].stalkIssuedPerBdv; // reads 0 (ReseedWhitelist runs later)
...
accountStalk += stalkIssuedPerBdv * totalBdvForAccount; // == 0
s.accts[deposits.accounts].stalk = accountStalk; // account reseeded with ~0 stalk

findings.impact: Every migrated Silo depositor is initialized on L2 with effectively zero base Stalk (instead of bdv * stalkIssuedPerBdv, normally >= 1 Stalk per BDV). Stalk is Beanstalk's core governance weight and the basis for Earned-Bean (root) accrual; reseeding it to ~0 silently strips all migrated holders of the voting power and yield entitlement they held on L1, while their deposit amounts/BDV are preserved. Protocol-wide accounting (per-account Stalk vs global stalk/roots) is left permanently inconsistent at genesis of the new chain.
findings.proof_of_concept:
Pipeline order (reseed/reseed.js -> reseed5..reseed7):
  reseed5: ReseedSilo.init  -> reseedSiloDeposit reads assetSettings[token].stalkIssuedPerBdv == 0
  reseed7: ReseedWhitelist.init -> LibWhitelist.whitelistToken sets assetSettings[token].stalkIssuedPerBdv = X
For a holder with totalBdvForAccount = B and all deposits at stemTip:
  accountStalk = 0 (grown) + 0 (= 0 * B) = 0
  s.accts[holder].stalk = 0   // expected: X * B
After reseed7 sets stalkIssuedPerBdv, ReseedSilo is never re-run, so the stalk stays 0.
findings.recommendation: Reorder the reseed pipeline so ReseedWhitelist (assetSettings population) runs BEFORE ReseedSilo, or have ReseedSilo carry the per-token stalkIssuedPerBdv in its own calldata struct (like it already does for stemTip/totalDeposited) instead of reading it from assetSettings. Add a post-reseed invariant check asserting sum(account.stalk) reconciles with sum(bdv * stalkIssuedPerBdv) + grown stalk for each token. Also reset s.accts[account].lastUpdate to the reseed season during ReseedSilo so the first post-migration _mow does not treat migrated accounts as season-0 (currently left at default 0 against a large season.current).

ite.intent: Strip every migrated L1 Silo depositor of their Stalk (governance weight + Earned-Bean accrual) at L2 genesis.
ite.technique: ReseedSilo.reseedSiloDeposit (reseed5) reads s.sys.silo.assetSettings[token].stalkIssuedPerBdv at ReseedSilo.sol#112, but that slot is only written by ReseedWhitelist.init (reseed7) via LibWhitelist.whitelistToken#161. At #161/#164 accountStalk = 0*totalBdvForAccount = 0 and is stored as the holder's entire Stalk; ReseedSilo never re-runs after whitelisting.
ite.evasion: The require() checks at #168-#175 only validate totalDeposited/totalDepositedBdv (amounts), not Stalk, so the zeroed-stalk state passes the only guard in the routine. There is no cross-step ordering assertion that assetSettings is populated before silo stalk is computed.

findings.title: L2 migration redeem replayable: no nonce, stalk and roots re-credited each call
findings.description: L2ContractMigrationFacet.redeemDepositsAndInternalBalances is a permissionless, one-time-intended migration routine for L1 contract-owned positions. It authorizes via (a) a Merkle proof over keccak256(owner, deposits, internalBalances, ownerRoots) and (b) an EIP-712 signature over (REDEEM_DEPOSIT_TYPE_HASH, owner, reciever, deadline). Neither path includes a nonce, and the function stores NO per-(owner) or per-(owner,reciever) 'already redeemed' marker — the Migration storage struct (System.sol#375) contains only `migratedL1Beans` and a buffer. Both the proof and the signature are fully deterministic for fixed inputs, so they remain valid until `deadline`. Because addMigratedDepositsToAccount writes deposits with `=` (idempotent) and overwrites mowStatuses, but setStalk (#205-#211) does `s.accts[reciever].stalk += accountStalk; s.accts[reciever].roots += accountRoots;` (INCREMENT), an attacker (or the receiver) can call the function repeatedly with the identical valid proof+signature before the deadline. Each replay re-adds the full accountStalk and ownerRoots while the deposit set stays fixed. This is an idempotency/lifecycle-ordering failure in a routine documented and named as a single redemption.
findings.impact: Stalk and Roots can be inflated without bound (up to the deadline) for the receiver of any migrating L1 contract. Stalk is governance weight and the denominator for Earned-Bean distribution; Roots directly entitle the holder to a pro-rata share of newly minted Beans. Replaying the redemption N times grants ~N x the legitimate stalk/roots, letting the receiver capture a disproportionate share of all future Bean mints and outvote the rest of the DAO, breaking the global stalk/roots conservation invariant and effectively draining yield from honest holders. Anyone can submit the replay since the proof and signature are public once the first redemption is broadcast.
findings.proof_of_concept:
1. Legitimate migrator broadcasts redeemDepositsAndInternalBalances(owner, reciever, deposits, ib, ownerRoots, proof, deadline, sig). Tx succeeds; reciever gets stalk S and roots R.
2. Attacker copies the identical calldata from the mempool/chain (no privileged setup, EOA tx).
3. Attacker re-submits the same call before `deadline`. verifyDepositsAndInternalBalances passes (proof unchanged), verifySignature passes (sig unchanged, block.timestamp <= deadline). deposits[id] re-written to same values; setStalk adds S, R again -> reciever stalk = 2S, roots = 2R.
4. Repeat until deadline -> stalk/roots = kS, kR with deposits still = original.
findings.recommendation: Record redemption completion: add a mapping (e.g. s.sys.migration redeemed[owner] or redeemed[keccak256(owner,reciever)]) set on first successful redemption and require(!redeemed[...]) at entry. Include a per-owner nonce in both the Merkle leaf and the EIP-712 struct hash. Make setStalk idempotent-safe (set vs add) or guard it behind the one-time marker. Bind the deposit/internalBalance payload into the signature (currently the signature covers only owner/reciever/deadline, while the proof covers the data — the two are not cross-bound).

ite.intent: Inflate a receiver's Stalk and Roots arbitrarily to capture a dominant share of Bean mints and DAO votes.
ite.technique: Re-submit the identical (proof, signature, deposits, ownerRoots) calldata of redeemDepositsAndInternalBalances multiple times before `deadline`; setStalk (L2ContractMigrationFacet.sol#206-207) increments stalk/roots on each call while there is no redeemed-marker and no nonce in either the Merkle leaf (#127) or the EIP-712 hash (#143-145).
ite.evasion: Developers relied on the Merkle proof + EIP-712 signature for authorization but provided no replay protection: the Migration struct (System.sol#375) has no per-account redeemed flag, and verifySignature only bounds expiry via `deadline`, which does not prevent reuse within the window.

findings.title: Migration redeem ignores verified internalBalances and zeroes global silo totals
findings.description: Two behavioral divergences in the same redemption routine. (1) Name/intent vs implementation: the function is named redeemDepositsAndInternalBalances and its @notice promises redemption of 'deposits and bean-asset internal balances'; the AccountInternalBalance[] internalBalances array is even committed into and validated by the Merkle leaf (verifyDepositsAndInternalBalances, #127-128). But the function body never credits internal balances anywhere — there is no write to s.accts[reciever].internalTokenBalance. Migrating contracts that present (and prove) internal balances have those balances silently dropped. (2) Cross-step global-state drift: addMigratedDepositsToAccount declares local `uint128 totalDeposited; uint128 totalDepositedBdv;` (#159-160) that are never incremented, then writes them to the GLOBAL aggregates `s.sys.silo.balances[token].deposited = totalDeposited;` and `.depositedBdv = totalDepositedBdv;` (#194-195) — i.e. it assigns 0, and uses `=` rather than `+=`. Any contract redemption therefore overwrites the global deposited/depositedBdv totals (set earlier by ReseedSilo) to 0 for that token, while the per-account deposit mappings remain populated. This makes the per-account deposits and the global silo balance permanently inconsistent across the migration lifecycle.

location.code_snippet:
uint128 totalDeposited;       // never incremented
uint128 totalDepositedBdv;    // never incremented
... (loop credits deposits per account but not internalBalances) ...
s.sys.silo.balances[depositData.token].deposited = totalDeposited;       // = 0, overwrites ReseedSilo global total
s.sys.silo.balances[depositData.token].depositedBdv = totalDepositedBdv; // = 0

findings.impact: Migrating L1 contracts permanently forfeit any internal (farm) balances they prove ownership of — those tokens are accounted nowhere on L2. Separately, the global s.sys.silo.balances[token].deposited / depositedBdv are reset to 0 by any contract redemption, desynchronizing global silo totals from the sum of per-account deposits set by ReseedSilo; downstream functions that read global deposited/depositedBdv (gauge/seed allocation, BDV-share math, totalDeposited getters) operate on corrupted aggregates. No reconciliation guard exists in this facet (unlike ReseedSilo's totals require()).
findings.proof_of_concept:
Internal balances dropped:
  redeemDepositsAndInternalBalances(owner, reciever, deposits, [ {token, 100} ], ...) with valid proof.
  After call: s.accts[reciever].internalTokenBalance[token] == 0 (never written). 100 lost.
Global totals zeroed:
  Before: s.sys.silo.balances[BEAN].deposited == T (from ReseedSilo).
  Any contract redemption for BEAN executes `s.sys.silo.balances[BEAN].deposited = 0;` (#194).
  After: global deposited == 0 while per-account deposit crates still sum to >0.
findings.recommendation: Credit internal balances: loop over internalBalances and set/add s.accts[reciever].internalTokenBalance[token] and the global internalTokenBalanceTotal (mirroring ReseedInternalBalances.setInternalBalances). For global silo totals, increment the running totalDeposited/totalDepositedBdv inside the deposit loop and apply them with `+=` to s.sys.silo.balances[token], not `=` with uninitialized zeros. Add a post-redemption reconciliation require() as ReseedSilo has.

ite.intent: Cause migrated contracts to lose internal balances and corrupt the protocol's global deposited totals during migration.
ite.technique: redeemDepositsAndInternalBalances validates internalBalances in the Merkle leaf (#127) but the body never credits them; addMigratedDepositsToAccount writes zero-initialized locals to the global aggregates s.sys.silo.balances[token].deposited/.depositedBdv with `=` (#194-195).
ite.evasion: The Merkle check authenticates the internalBalances payload, creating the appearance they are processed; no invariant/require ties the global silo totals to the sum of credited per-account deposits in this facet, so the zeroing passes silently.
